title: Fathom

evidence.layout: Pointer table at CPU $FA6F, 28 phrases with a final end bound, command-ordered. Every phrase parses and terminates in a stop frame.
evidence.table_between_phrases: This set puts the pointer table BETWEEN its speech: entries 0-26 run from $E000 up to $F77D, below the table at $FA6F, and entry 27 points at $FAD3, above it. The phrase below the table would otherwise run through it to reach the one above. Understudy clamps every phrase at the table, which is why this layout works.
evidence.independent_check: Frame count agrees with a separately built corpus: platform_lpc_frames.csv records 1192 frames across 28 streams for fathom, matching this layout exactly. The 28th stream, 9 frames at $FAD3, is the one above the table -- reading only the 27 below it gives 1183 and is how the layout was found to be short.
evidence.conversion: 1192 frames converted, all keeping their frame kind when the output was re-parsed with the target tables.
evidence.emulation: The converted devices were loaded into a simulation of the Squawk & Talk board, which booted and issued the same 8 SPEAK EXTERNAL commands as the original set.
evidence.not_verified: No converted ROM from this profile has been played on a real board. Nobody has heard it.

notes: This sound ROM set is shared by 3 game revisions: fathom, fathoma, fathomb.
The pointer table sits between the speech, not above or below it.
